title: Self-ordering anodized-alumina pores as litho-free capacitor molds
idea: Ideal: capacitor holes that pattern themselves. Closest: anodize a thick Al film over the cell array, seeded by shallow DUV-imprinted dimples on the storage-contact grid, so it self-orders into the same honeycomb lattice DRAM already uses (25-35 nm pitch, >100:1 pores); ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines the pores, replacing the capacitor-mold lithography and high-aspect-ratio dry etch.
why: Facts 1 and 4: removes one critical litho layer and the most expensive HAR plasma etch; AR ~115 becomes cheap, so Cs +40-50%; est. 5-8% wafer-cost cut in the capacitor module.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching digs 150:1 capacitor holes without plasma
idea: Ideal: holes that dig themselves to any depth. Closest: a DSA-patterned Pt or Ag catalyst mesh sinks into a thick poly-Si mold in HF/H2O2 at room temperature (MacEtch), cutting straight 150:1 holes; the catalyst is stripped, the mold oxidized/lined and used as the capacitor template.
why: Facts 1 and 4: replaces $10M+ cryogenic HAR etchers (and their helium backside cooling) with wet benches; AR 115+ affordable for Cs ~8 fF; capacitor-module capex roughly -40%.

title: Two-height nanoimprint template prints wordline trench and contact together
idea: Ideal: one stamp prints the whole cell. Closest: an e-beam master is replicated into two-height nanoimprint templates that imprint buried-wordline trenches and bitline-contact recesses in one resist step (dual-damascene in resist); array layers imprint only, periphery stays on DUV.
why: Fact 4: replaces 2-3 EUV exposures in the array with one NIL step at ~1/10 the tool capex, and the self-registered two-level pattern deletes one overlay budget; ~15-20% litho cost cut.

title: Vicinal-wafer atomic steps template sub-15 nm wordline lines
idea: Ideal: the crystal itself is the mask. Closest: anneal a miscut Si surface so atomic steps bunch into a periodic ridge array with a 10-20 nm period set by the miscut angle; area-selective deposition decorates the step edges into a hardmask for wordline lines across the whole wafer, with one DUV cut mask for line ends.
why: Fact 4: dense line/space with zero EUV and none of SAQP's 10+ deposition/etch loops; pitch is set by crystallography, not optics.

title: Stack depreciated-node DRAM wafers instead of buying an EUV node
idea: Ideal: more density with no new tools. Closest: keep fully depreciated DUV-only 1x-nm-class DRAM lines running, thin complete wafers to ~3 um and hybrid-bond 4-8 of them into a monolithic stack with a fine-pitch vertical bus, so bits per footprint come from tier count while every tier runs on paid-off equipment.
why: Fact 4 and capital: depreciation (~55% of wafer cost) falls toward ~15%; 8 tiers at half density = 4x bits per footprint; comparable cost/bit with near-zero new capex and no $15B fab.

title: Ashable carbon capacitor mold removed dry, ending pillar collapse
idea: Ideal: the capacitor mold vanishes without touching the pillars. Closest: build the pillar mold from amorphous carbon instead of oxide, so after electrode ALD it is removed by an O2/N2 plasma ash rather than an HF dip-out, eliminating capillary pillar collapse, supercritical-CO2 drying and the nitride support-mesh lithography.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR can rise from ~70 toward ~100 without collapse (Cs +30-40%), deletes one mask (support mesh) plus wet/dry steps, and removes a top yield-excursion source.

title: Sealed vacuum wafer backbone replaces the ISO-3 cleanroom ballroom
idea: Ideal: no cleanroom at all. Closest: wafers travel only through a linear vacuum/N2 tunnel that docks every tool (an extended cluster-tool backbone with mag-lev carriers), so the building needs ISO 8 air, not ISO 3-4 fan-filter ceilings, and queue-time oxidation disappears.
why: Fab capital: cleanroom shell and HVAC are ~20-30% of fab cost and a large energy/water load; est. $2-3B saved per fab and faster construction.

title: Park the dielectric at its antiferroelectric transition for k above 100
idea: Ideal: a dielectric with infinite k so the capacitor needs no height. Closest: an antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich HfZrO film whose field-induced AFE-to-FE transition is centered at the plate bias, so the small storage-voltage swing rides the steep part of the P-E curve for k_eff ~100-150.
why: Fact 1: k ~70 is the stated requirement; at k_eff ~100 pillar AR drops from ~70:1 to ~30:1, deleting the hardest etch/deposition loops and the anti-collapse support layers.

title: Freeze one array mask set; multibeam writes all periphery variants
idea: Ideal: masks cost nothing. Closest: freeze a single array reticle set for every product and density, and write the product-specific periphery and option layers with a massively parallel multi-e-beam direct-write tool, so new SKUs, CXL/PIM variants and bug fixes need zero new reticles.
why: Fact 4: leading-edge mask sets cost $20-40M and months; zero-NRE derivatives make niche and custom DRAM profitable and speed fixes.

title: Open-licensed DRAM array IP lets any foundry make commodity memory
idea: Ideal: every fab can make DRAM. Closest: a consortium develops a proven 6F2 array plus process-module recipes validated on 2-3 foundries' tool sets and licenses them per wafer (an ARM model for memory), so logic foundries add DRAM lines without a decade of process R&D.
why: Capital/time and U.S. manufacturability: entry cost falls to tool spend only; adds suppliers to a three-vendor oligopoly.

title: Shared EUV hub exposes critical layers for many small DRAM fabs
idea: Ideal: EUV is free for small makers. Closest: a central EUV hub exposes only the 5-7 critical layers of wafers shipped in sealed N2 FOUPs from several smaller DRAM fabs that do all DUV, deposition and etch locally, with tolling priced per layer.
why: Fact 4 and capital: $200-380M scanners are pooled at high utilization; a new entrant skips EUV capex, roughly -30% entry capital.

title: Selective-area ALD grows storage contact and bottom electrode as one
idea: Ideal: contact and capacitor are one object made in one step. Closest: inhibitor SAMs on oxide let TiN or Ru ALD/CVD nucleate only on doped-Si landing pads and grow bottom-up through the mold, forming the storage-node plug and the capacitor bottom electrode continuously with no CMP or recess.
why: Facts 4 and 7: deletes one litho layer, one CMP, one etch-back plus metrology; removes an interface that adds contact resistance; ~3-5% fewer steps.

title: Capacitor-first wafer with transferred silicon film for transistors on top
idea: Ideal: the capacitor never competes with the transistor for space or heat. Closest: etch and fill deep capacitors in a bulk wafer first, anneal the high-k at >1000 C for its highest-k phase, then Smart-Cut-bond a thin single-crystal Si film on top and build access transistors aligned to the buried capacitor contacts.
why: Facts 1 and 4: capacitor depth is no longer limited by stack height or thermal budget, high-k phase gives Cs gains, and the capacitor module can run in a separate, less advanced line.

title: Catalyst-grown vertical nanowire forests replace etched capacitor pillars
idea: Ideal: capacitor pillars that build themselves upward. Closest: DSA-placed catalyst dots on each storage contact seed vertical vapor-liquid-solid growth of doped-Si nanowires to 1-1.5 um; TiN, high-k and top plate are ALD-wrapped around them, so there is no mold, HAR etch or wet dip-out.
why: Facts 1 and 4: AR set by growth time, not etch physics; removes mold deposition, HAR etch and collapse-prone drying; capacitor module step count roughly halved.

title: Material-contrast self-alignment lets each layer inherit the one below
idea: Ideal: one lithography step for the whole cell stack. Closest: after the active area is defined, each later layer (wordline cap, bitline, storage contact) is placed by selective deposition and selective etch chemistries keyed to the material contrast of the layer beneath, so only line-cut masks remain.
why: Fact 4: critical masks per cell ~7 to ~3, zero edge-placement error between inherited layers, ~50% less EUV dependence.

title: Passive RF resonators let every wafer report its own metrology
idea: Ideal: zero metrology tools. Closest: scribe lines carry passive LC resonators built from the layers made so far, whose resonance shifts with CD, film thickness and overlay; a contactless RF reader in each load port interrogates every wafer in seconds after each module, replacing sampled CD-SEM/OCD for go/no-go.
why: Fact 4: metrology/inspection is ~10-15% of fab capex and adds cycle time; 100% wafer coverage catches excursions days earlier and raises yield.

title: Factory-built cleanroom pods shrink DRAM fab build to 18 months
idea: Ideal: a fab appears overnight. Closest: standardize a 10k-wafer-per-month DRAM module as transportable prefabricated cleanroom and subfab skids, with tools installed and qualified at the module factory, then shipped and craned onto a slab; capacity grows pod by pod.
why: Capital/time: build time 3-5 years to ~1.5; smaller increments cut risk and let U.S. sites avoid megaproject labor shortages.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling with palladium recovery replaces scarce helium
idea: Ideal: etch and deposition need no helium. Closest: switch electrostatic-chuck backside gas to H2 (thermal conductivity close to He) at sub-flammable volumes, with a Pd-membrane capture-and-reuse loop on each tool; keep He only where H2 chemistry is incompatible.
why: Resource chokepoint (Qatar helium offline): DRAM etch/deposition are heavy He users; cuts He demand ~70-90%.

title: Kerfless epitaxial lift-off wafers end high-purity quartz crucible dependence
idea: Ideal: wafers without crucibles. Closest: grow 50-100 um epitaxial Si on a porous-Si release layer of a reusable parent wafer, peel and bond it to a cheap carrier, and reuse the parent 30-50 times, so one Czochralski crucible supports ~50x more wafers.
why: Resource chokepoint (Spruce Pine HPQ >80%): DRAM uses only the top few um of silicon; also cuts polysilicon energy per wafer.

title: Fully silicided polysilicon buried wordlines eliminate tungsten fill
idea: Ideal: wordlines that need no imported metal. Closest: fill the buried-wordline trench with in-situ-doped amorphous Si and fully convert it with a self-limiting Ni silicidation anneal (FUSI, as in fully silicided gates), skipping WF6 CVD, W etch-back and W CMP.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and Fact 4: removes W deposition tools and steps; NiSi ~15 uOhm-cm is competitive with thin W in narrow trenches.

title: Halve EUV dose by designing arrays to absorb stochastic defects
idea: Ideal: EUV throughput doubles for free. Closest: expose array layers at ~30 mJ/cm2 instead of ~60, accepting more stochastic micro-bridges and missing contacts, and absorb them with column/row spares, per-sub-array ECC and a repair map designed in from day one.
why: Fact 4: EUV is the bottleneck tool; ~1.6-1.8x scanner throughput means fewer $150M+ scanners per 10k wafer starts.

title: One logic die multiplexes periphery for four bonded array dies
idea: Ideal: periphery costs nothing. Closest: leave only bitline sense amps and local drivers on array dies, and move decoders, I/O, DLL, refresh and ECC logic to one 28 nm logic die that time-multiplexes four stacked array dies through fine-pitch hybrid bonds.
why: Fact 7: periphery is ~49% of the die; sharing it 1:4 cuts total silicon per bit ~30-35% and moves logic to cheaper non-DRAM fabs.

title: Free-electron-laser EUV source feeds a whole fab of scanners
idea: Ideal: EUV photons as cheap as DUV. Closest: one energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser produces multi-kW EUV, split by grazing-incidence optics to 10-20 scanners, replacing per-tool tin-droplet plasma sources.
why: Fact 4: source power limits throughput; ~3-5x power per scanner, no tin debris, lower energy per exposed wafer across a DRAM fab's EUV layers.

title: CFET-stacked two-transistor gain cell from an unmodified logic flow
idea: Ideal: memory that costs zero extra masks in a logic fab. Closest: in a CFET (n-over-p stacked nanosheet) process, the top sheet is a high-Vt write transistor and the bottom sheet a read transistor whose gate is the storage node, giving a capacitorless 2T gain cell in one transistor footprint using only a layout change.
why: Facts 1 and 4, U.S. manufacturability: zero added steps and no capacitor module; any CFET logic fab, including U.S. ones, becomes a DRAM-class source; ~2x denser than planar 2T eDRAM.

title: Single-mask vertical thyristor pillars cut from blanket p-n-p-n epitaxy
idea: Ideal: a cell patterned by one exposure. Closest: grow a blanket p-n-p-n Si/SiGe epitaxial stack, cut it into 4F2 pillars with one DSA-assisted hole pattern, and form a self-aligned spacer gate on the p-base; the regenerative thyristor latch stores the bit with no capacitor.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: deletes the capacitor module (~25% of DRAM steps), 4F2 instead of 6F2, ~1 critical array mask; uA read currents simplify sensing.

title: SiGe quantum wells inside 3D tier stack hold the bit
idea: Ideal: the 3D DRAM's own epitaxial layers are the memory. Closest: in the Si/SiGe superlattice used to build 3D tiers, leave a thin SiGe well inside each Si channel layer as a hole pocket (~200 meV valence-band offset), turning every lateral transistor into a floating-body 1T cell so the lateral capacitor is never built.
why: Fact 2: removes the lateral-capacitor module that blocks 3D DRAM; each tier is one transistor tall, so >26 tiers come with roughly half the steps per tier.

title: 3D-NAND toolset builds channel-hole gain cells with no EUV
idea: Ideal: density from tier count with tools already paid for. Closest: in a NAND-style oxide/word-plate stack, each channel hole holds two concentric ALD oxide-semiconductor devices per tier: an outer write channel charging an isolated metal ring, and an inner read channel gated by that ring, so every tier crossing is a capacitorless 2T gain cell built with the 3D NAND etch, ALD and staircase flow.
why: Facts 2 and 4: 100+ tiers at DUV pitch in existing NAND fabs with no capacitor and no EUV; bit cost could follow NAND-like layer economics if speed and retention hold.

title: Film-thickness-defined vertical gain cells need only immersion lithography
idea: Ideal: every critical dimension set by deposition, none by light. Closest: vertical write-over-read transistors in one pillar whose channel lengths equal deposited spacer thicknesses and gate lengths equal ALD metal thicknesses; only pillar placement uses 193i at ~40 nm half pitch, giving a ~4F2 capacitorless 2T gain cell.
why: Fact 4: zero EUV layers and angstrom-level CD control from ALD; with no capacitor the cell is ~300 nm tall instead of ~1.5 um, so fewer deep etches.

title: Stacked resonant-tunneling-diode latch replaces the storage capacitor
idea: Ideal: a cell that holds its state forever with one transistor. Closest: grow two series resonant-tunneling diodes (Si/SiGe or InGaAs/AlAs) as blanket epitaxy over the access-transistor contact (a Goto pair); their N-shaped I-V gives two stable storage-node voltages held by valley current, patterned with the same contact mask.
why: Facts 1 and 3: no capacitor and no refresh (saves ~46 fJ/bit and 10-20% bandwidth); one epi step replaces ~20 capacitor steps; needs peak-to-valley >10 at nA levels.

title: Prestressed buckled nanobeam stores bits as mechanical states
idea: Ideal: a bit that needs no charge at all. Closest: a 200 nm compressively stressed SiN or amorphous-carbon beam released over a BEOL cavity buckles up or down; side electrodes snap it in ~10 ns (GHz resonance) and a non-contact capacitive sense reads position, so the state is held mechanically with zero leakage and no wear.
why: Facts 3 and 4: no capacitor, no refresh, zero standby power; BEOL-only on any logic wafer with 3-4 DUV masks plus a release step.

title: Liquid-nitrogen operation turns logic gain cells into seconds-retention memory
idea: Ideal: a transistor that never leaks, so no capacitor is needed. Closest: run capacitorless 2T/3T Si gain cells made in standard logic fabs at 77 K in LN2-cooled memory sleds, where subthreshold and junction leakage fall by >10^6 and retention rises from ~50 us to seconds.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: memory from logic fabs with zero added masks; refresh nearly vanishes; cryocooler energy is the trade, offset by lower wire resistance.

title: Wafer vendor ships memory substrates with buried back-gate planes
idea: Ideal: the memory maker buys a wafer that is already half a memory. Closest: a bonded Smart-Cut substrate with a buried n+ back-gate plane under thin BOX and a 10 nm Si film; the fab runs a plain planar logic flow and gets double-gate floating-body 1T cells whose negative back-gate holds stored holes, with no capacitor.
why: Facts 1, 4, 7: removes ~25-30% of DRAM front-end steps and shifts that work to cheap substrate-bonding lines; lets FD-SOI-style logic fabs make 1T memory.

title: Charge-coupled shift-register memory revived with spacer-patterned gates
idea: Ideal: a memory with no per-cell transistor and no capacitor. Closest: rebuild 1970s CCD memory as many short (32-64-bit) recirculating loops of overlapping gate electrodes formed by self-aligned double patterning on DUV; charge packets in surface potential wells are clocked past one shared sense/restore amplifier per loop.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4, 7: removes access transistors and capacitors, makes refresh part of recirculation, ~2-3F2 per bit at DUV pitch; ~20-30 ns average latency at GHz clocking, with clocking energy as the main risk.

title: Ion-implant isolation defines MRAM bits without etching the stack
idea: Ideal: magnetic bits with no etch of the magnetic stack. Closest: deposit a blanket perpendicular MTJ film and define cells with a masked light-ion plus oxygen implant that kills anisotropy and makes the inter-bit film resistive, leaving a planar, unetched stack with no redeposition or sidewall shorts.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: no capacitor or refresh; removes the MTJ ion-beam etch that limits MRAM pitch and yield, so pitch could shrink toward ~30 nm; 10^12+ endurance with VCMA writing.

title: Self-assembled nanocrystal monolayer forms storage nodes without patterning
idea: Ideal: storage nodes that place themselves. Closest: a spin- or Langmuir-Blodgett-assembled monolayer of 5 nm Ru nanocrystals over a ~1.5 nm tunnel oxide on the transistor channel; each cell gate overlaps ~20 dots that hold charge (ms retention, ns direct-tunneling write at ~1.5 V), with no lithography for the nodes.
why: Facts 1 and 4: no capacitor; storage-node formation is a single coating step; direct tunneling instead of Fowler-Nordheim avoids oxide wear and targets high endurance.

title: Selector-only chalcogenide crosspoint decks at two masks per layer
idea: Ideal: a cell that is just a wire crossing. Closest: one amorphous chalcogenide threshold-switch layer at each crosspoint whose threshold voltage is set by write polarity (selector-only memory); each deck needs two DUV line masks, decks stack 4-8 high over CMOS, with no capacitor and no transistor per cell.
why: Facts 1, 4, 7: 4F2 per deck with DUV-only patterning and periphery under the array; endurance must reach 10^12+ for DRAM duty, an honest risk.

title: Open capacitorless memory macro qualified at every U.S. logic fab
idea: Ideal: every fab already in the country is a memory fab. Closest: a CHIPS-funded open PDK macro (gain-cell array, sense amps, refresh controller) qualified on Intel 18A, TSMC Arizona, GlobalFoundries and SkyWater flows, so any U.S. chip can carry hundreds of MB on-die and GB-class stacked working memory without a DRAM fab.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: zero new fab capex; turns logic wafer starts into memory supply and cuts off-chip DRAM demand for caches and KV buffers.

title: Grayscale exposure etches every 3D tier contact in one step
idea: Ideal: a 3D array whose tier contacts cost one step. Closest: for a capacitorless 3D floating-body or gain-cell stack, replace the multi-mask trim-and-etch wordline staircase with one grayscale (variable-dose) exposure that makes a resist ramp of N heights; a proportional etch transfers it, opening every tier's landing at once.
why: Facts 2 and 4: staircases cost one litho/etch loop per 4-8 tiers plus array-edge area; a single ramp removes ~10-20 masks at 64+ tiers, and thin capacitorless tiers keep the ramp shallow.

title: Wafer-scale capacitorless memory bonded face-to-face onto compute wafers
idea: Ideal: memory with no package, dicing or interposer. Closest: a full 300 mm wafer of logic-process gain-cell memory is hybrid-bonded wafer-to-wafer onto a wafer-scale accelerator; defective memory tiles are routed around by the compute wafer's network and test happens once per wafer pair.
why: Facts 5 and 6: removes the HBM TSV tax (~3x area/bit) and interposer/packaging capex; data movement <0.5 pJ/bit; yield loss handled by architecture.

title: Self-amplifying floating-base bipolar cell needs no sense amplifiers
idea: Ideal: a cell loud enough that the periphery disappears. Closest: a vertical npn whose floating p-base stores holes; on read, the stored charge switches on bipolar gain (beta ~50-100) for uA-level bitline current, so simple inverter sensing replaces pitch-matched differential sense amps, with no capacitor anywhere.
why: Fact 7 and Fact 4: periphery is ~49% of the die; relaxed sense-amp pitch rules shrink it and let it move to a cheaper process; reads need no charge sharing.

title: Four-level gain cells double bits without a lithography node
idea: Ideal: more bits from the same pattern. Closest: store four charge levels on the read-transistor gate of a capacitorless gain cell, exploiting its non-destructive current read with a time-to-threshold sensing ADC per sub-array, and refresh only the inner levels that drift first.
why: Fact 4: 2 bits/cell equals several 10-20% node shrinks with zero new tools or masks.

title: All-dry, water-lean flow enabled once capacitor dip-out vanishes
idea: Ideal: a memory fab with no ultrapure water. Closest: with no capacitor mold to wet-strip (the HF dip-out and supercritical drying that dominate DRAM wet work), run the capacitorless cell flow on vapor-HF, remote-plasma and cryogenic-aerosol cleans with gas recycling, keeping UPW only for CMP.
why: Resources (water, energy) and capex: UPW plants and wet benches are ~$1B per fab; ~50-70% less UPW opens arid U.S. sites.

title: Fifteen-day cycle-time capacitorless line sells memory build-to-order
idea: Ideal: memory made on demand, with no inventory or price swings. Closest: a ~30-mask capacitorless flow on single-wafer tools only (RTP instead of furnaces, no 12-hour batch ALD) targets 15-20-day fab cycle time versus ~90, and sells capacity as monthly build-to-order contracts.
why: Capital and supply: far less WIP (~$1B per fab tied up today) and supply that tracks AI demand monthly, damping 4x price spikes.

title: Self-restoring keeper transistor makes gain cell quasi-static, refresh-free
idea: Ideal: a dynamic cell that refreshes itself. Closest: add to a 2T gain cell a minimum-size keeper transistor gated by the read node, whose subthreshold current tops the storage node up toward its own stored rail faster than the access device leaks it away, so the capacitorless cell holds data without refresh.
why: Fact 3 and Fact 4: no refresh and no leakage-tail screening, which relaxes implant/anneal control and cuts retention test time (a major test cost).

title: Laser-crystallized silicon tiers stack refresh-free SRAM toward DRAM density
idea: Ideal: a static, refresh-free cell at DRAM density. Closest: monolithically stack 6-8 tiers of thin single-grain Si, crystallized by pulsed-laser melting of amorphous Si at <450 C wafer temperature, with n and p halves of each SRAM cell on alternate tiers, so bits per footprint multiply with no capacitor and DUV-friendly 28 nm rules.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: no capacitor, no refresh, standard logic tools plus laser anneal; honestly still ~4-8x below DRAM per area today, so the target is cache and buffer tiers.

title: Nanosecond protonic gain cell stores bits as ions, BEOL-only
idea: Ideal: memory where nothing leaks because the state is atoms, not electrons. Closest: a BEOL transistor whose MoO3 or TiO2 channel conductance is set by nanosecond proton insertion from a thin solid electrolyte (PSG) gate, giving a volatile-to-hours state with non-destructive read; three DUV masks at <400 C, no capacitor.
why: Facts 1, 3, 4: no capacitor and slow refresh, stackable in BEOL tiers on any logic wafer; tungsten-free channel avoids the W chokepoint.
